newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM sees 1997 land sales raising $10 billion.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM sees 1997 land sales raising $10 billion.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday he expected the sale of state-owned lands to raise $10 billion during 1997.
"This month $500 million will be made from the sale of real estate. While $10 billion will be made in the year," Erbakan said in a speech to his Islamist Welfare Party.
He also said a second-hand car import scheme introduced since his coalition came to power late last June has brought foreign currency deposits worth $1.15 billion to Turkish banks.

He said around 30,000 applications to import cars have been accepted under the scheme which allows Turkish citizens to bring in cars duty free if they deposit 50,000 marks at a Turkish bank for a year. Machinery has also been imported under the scheme.
The Prime Minister told deputies from his party that a state account opened to pool the resources of public companies currently holds 600 trillion Turkish lira.
The pool account, car scheme and state land sales are part of a series of measures introduced by Erbakan in revenue-raising packages aimed at raising funds to plug the country's large deficits.
